sections.h2: What kind of place is Meriwether County for a seller?
sections.html:
Meriwether County is a rural county in west central Georgia, counted inside the Atlanta metro area, with Greenville as the county seat and Manchester as its largest city. The General Assembly formed it on December 14, 1827, as the 73rd county in the state and named it for David Meriwether, a Revolutionary War general who later sat in Congress, according to Wikipedia.

The county covers 505 square miles, almost all of it land. It lies in the Piedmont, and the Pine Mountain range rises in the south near Warm Springs and Manchester. The eastern two thirds drains into the Upper Flint River basin, while the western third runs toward Lake Harding on the Chattahoochee. Coweta, Spalding, Pike, Upson, Talbot, Harris and Troup counties all touch its borders.

Greenville, Luthersville, Manchester, Warm Springs and Woodbury are cities. Gay, Lone Oak and Pine Mountain are towns, and Pine Mountain sits mostly in Harris County. Alvaton is unincorporated. The Meriwether County School District runs six campuses: Mountain View Elementary, Unity Elementary, Greenville Middle, Manchester Middle, Greenville High and Manchester High. A lot inside Manchester and a farm on a county road land on one county bill, while a lot in the Town of Gay adds a separate city bill.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Meriwether County housing?
sections.html:
Most Meriwether County homes are lived in by their owners: the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page shows a 73.0% owner rate for 2020 to 2024 and a median home value of $168,800.

Population fell from 21,992 in 2010 to 20,613 in the 2020 count, then rose 4.4% by mid 2025. Residents 65 and older make up 23.8% of the county, and 17.8% of people live below the poverty line. Long drives to work and modest incomes shape how buyers here read a tax bill, so a seller who can show a paid-up account has an easier conversation.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Meriwether County?
sections.html:
The Meriwether County Tax Commissioner bills and collects every property tax bill, and the office sits at 17234 Roosevelt Highway, Building A, in Greenville. Its county tax site lists (706) 672-4219, weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and a mailing address of PO Box 729, Greenville, GA 30222.

That office sets neither values nor rates. The Board of Tax Assessors appraises property and can be reached at (706) 672-4222. A Board of Equalization, appointed by the grand jury, hears value appeals. The county commission and the school board each adopt a millage rate, and one mill equals $1 for every $1,000 of assessed value.

Residents of Luthersville, Manchester, Warm Springs, Woodbury, Greenville and Lone Oak pay city and county tax together to the county commissioner. The Town of Gay collects its own city tax, so a Gay owner pays the county here and the town separately. The tax site also has tabs for tax sales and excess funds.

sections.h2: When are Meriwether County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property bills in Meriwether County are due December 20. The commissioner's site says bills normally go in the mail by October 1 and asks anyone without one by October 15 to call the office.

  • Real estate and business personal property: December 20.
  • Mobile homes: April 1, with the decal posted by that date.
  • Boats: November 15, after May assessment notices and a 45 day appeal window.
  • Other personal property: bills usually go out in mid November.
  • Motor vehicles: due by the owner's birthday.

Georgia's Department of Revenue explains that counties may move the official date to December 1 or November 15 or bill in installments, and that interest cannot start until 60 days after the postmark of the bill. Read the date printed on your own bill before you plan a closing around it.

sections.h2: What does a late Meriwether County bill cost?
sections.html:
A late real estate bill in Meriwether County picks up interest from the day after the due date and a stacking penalty. The tax site says the interest rate on real and personal property changes from year to year, so ask the office for the current figure.

  • Penalty on real and personal property: 5% on the 120th day after each due date, and another 5% every 120 days after that, up to 20%.
  • Mobile homes: a single 10% penalty the day after the due date, plus interest at 1%.
  • Lien: once tax sits unpaid more than 90 days, a FiFa is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, and credit bureaus can see it.

The office accepts partial payments, though interest keeps running on the unpaid balance. A buyer's title search will find a recorded lien, so clearing it before listing keeps a sale on schedule.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Meriwether County tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay in person, online, by mail or through the drop box in front of the building. In the office the commissioner takes checks, cash and cards, and online payments run through the tax site by card or PayPal.

  • Online card payments carry a convenience fee of 2.57% or $1.50, whichever is larger.
  • Card payments in the office or by phone carry 3.00% or $1.50 minimum.
  • Mail checks to Meriwether County Tax Commissioner, PO Box 729, Greenville, GA 30222, with the parcel or account number on the check.

If a mortgage company pays your taxes, the office will give tax information to that lender on request. The site suggests forwarding your bill coupons to the lender with a short note, so the lender knows what to pay.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Meriwether County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice to appeal a Meriwether County value. The county tax site says notices usually mail in the spring, and the appeal must be in writing, filed first with the Board of Tax Assessors, naming the method you choose.

The grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption. You may go to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, and the Department of Revenue also lists a hearing officer as a third route. After a decision, a taxpayer can carry the case to superior court by giving the assessors written notice. Property owners can also file a return between January 1 and April 1 to state their own value, which sets up appeal rights if the board raises it.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply to a Meriwether County home?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the main one, and it requires you to own and live in the house on January 1. Applications must arrive before April 1 to count for that year, and a later filing starts the exemption the next year.

First-time owners should bring a warranty deed, and the driver's license must show the Meriwether County street address, because a post office box is not accepted. Once granted, the exemption renews on its own until you move. The county FAQ notes an additional exemption at age 62. Business owners can ask about the freeport exemption on inventory, and the county tax site says the assessors make the final call on eligibility. Ask the Tax Assessor's office about conservation use or other special programs.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when a Meriwether County house sells?
sections.html:
The owner on January 1 is responsible for that year's tax, even if the house sells in January. The Department of Revenue says Georgia law gives no refund to partial-year owners, so the split between buyer and seller is a matter for the contract and the closing statement.

Before closing, ask the tax commissioner for the current balance on the parcel, including any penalty or lien. A seller with delinquent tax can have it paid from the sale proceeds at closing, which is how most liens come off the title. If the sale closes before the bill is mailed in the fall, ask the closing attorney how the year is being handled.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Meriwether County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the tax commissioner at (706) 672-4219 for billing and payment questions. For a question about your property's value, call the Tax Assessor's office at (706) 672-4222.

faqs.q: What day is the Meriwether County real estate bill due?
faqs.a: December 20 is the due date for real estate and business personal property. Bills normally mail by October 1, and the county asks owners without a bill by October 15 to call.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Meriwether County bill online?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax site accepts cards and PayPal, with a fee of 2.57% or $1.50 minimum. You can also pay in the office, by mail or at the drop box outside the building.

faqs.q: Does selling my Meriwether County house cancel the year's tax?
faqs.a: No. The January 1 owner is liable for the whole year, and Georgia law gives no refund for part of a year. Settle the split in the sales contract.

faqs.q: How long do I have to challenge a Meriwether County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. File a written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors and say whether you want the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.
